# OpenMemoryOptimizer

> OpenMemoryOptimizer is a free, open-source memory (RAM) optimizer for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit), written in Rust and licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. It frees memory that open apps and Windows hold but are not using, in one click, automatically when memory runs low or on a timer, or on a schedule. No ads, no account, no tracking, no network access.

Key facts:

- Price: free. No paid tier.
- Platform: Windows 10 and Windows 11, 64-bit. Not available for macOS or Linux.
- Distribution: installer (`OpenMemoryOptimizer-Setup-<version>.exe`) or portable zip (`OpenMemoryOptimizer-win64.zip`), with `SHA256SUMS.txt` in every release.
- Requires administrator rights: Windows only lets elevated programs free memory held by other apps and clear cached memory.
- Not code-signed yet: Windows SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC"; choose More info, then Run anyway.
- Interface languages: English and Brazilian Portuguese.
- Author: Lucian Caetano.

## What a cleanup does

Steps run in this order; optional ones can be turned off:

1. Clear clipboard (optional).
2. Deep clean (optional): briefly allocates up to 1 GB to push unused data out of memory.
3. Free memory from open apps: trims the working sets of running processes.
4. Clear cached memory (optional): purges the Windows standby list.
5. Trim the system file cache.

It then waits 3 seconds and reports the memory actually freed. Automatic cleanup triggers when free memory falls below a chosen threshold (checked every 5 minutes, optionally only when CPU is idle) or every N minutes. Scheduled cleanups use Windows Task Scheduler (daily, weekly, monthly, at sign-in or when idle).
